description: Personal calendar and scheduling assistant with event search, next-event lookup, and event detail tools.

tools.name: find_events
tools.description: Search the user's calendar events. Returns events whose start time falls in [start_time, end_time). Both bounds are required and must be UTC ISO 8601 strings (e.g. 2026-07-01T04:00:00Z); start is inclusive, end is exclusive.

params.name: query
params.description: Free-text title or attendee filter (optional; empty returns all events in range)

tools.name: get_next_event
tools.description: Return the user's next upcoming calendar event (the first event starting after the current moment). Takes no arguments.

tools.name: get_event_details
tools.description: Return full details for a single calendar event, looked up by its event id.

params.name: event_id
params.description: The calendar event id, e.g. evt-1234

scenarios.title: this-coming-tuesday-schedule
scenarios.user: What's on my calendar this coming Tuesday?

checks.note: Must include the Tuesday 8:30pm dinner (UTC-day Jul 22); must not include Monday-night pottery (UTC-day Jul 21) or the week-after Tax advisor call

scenarios.rationale: Now = THURSDAY Jul 16 2026, 9:30am EDT (UTC-4). 'This coming Tuesday' pins the nearest upcoming Tuesday = Jul 21 (the wording disambiguates against the week-after reading; nl2time agrees: [2026-07-21T04:00Z, 2026-07-22T04:00Z)). Civil day Tue Jul 21 in NY = [Jul 21 00:00 ET, Jul 22 00:00 ET) = [2026-07-21T04:00Z, 2026-07-22T04:00Z). In range: Team standup 13:30Z = 9:30am EDT, Marketing sync 19:00Z = 3:00pm EDT, Dinner with Sam 2026-07-22T00:30Z = Tue Jul 21 8:30pm EDT (UTC day Jul 22 — dropped by naive UTC-day bounds). Excluded: Pottery class 2026-07-21T00:00Z = MON Jul 20 8:00pm EDT (UTC day Jul 21 — wrongly included by naive UTC-day bounds), Budget sync today Thu Jul 16, Tax advisor call Tue Jul 28 (week after). get_next_event is mocked consistently: next event after now is the 11:00am Budget sync today.

scenarios.title: tomorrow-morning-meetings
scenarios.user: How many meetings do I have tomorrow morning?

checks.note: Standup 9:00am + 1:1 11:00am PDT; the 12:30pm lunch is afternoon and Trivia night (2026-07-15T04:00Z) is TONIGHT 9pm PDT, not tomorrow
Trivia night's UTC timestamp reads tomorrow-morning-ish (04:00Z Jul 15) but it is Tuesday 9:00pm PDT tonight

scenarios.rationale: Now = TUESDAY Jul 14 2026, 8:00am PDT (UTC-7). Tomorrow = civil Wednesday Jul 15 in LA. Window grading (core/envelope per the 2026-07-26 blind-audit adjudication): CORE = minimal round-local-hour interval containing both intended rows (standup 9:00am, 1:1 11:00am PDT) = [09:00, 12:00) PDT = [2026-07-15T16:00Z, 2026-07-15T19:00Z). ENVELOPE = the morning policy window [00:00, 12:00) PDT on Wed Jul 15 = [2026-07-15T07:00Z, 2026-07-15T19:00Z) (no now-extension: now is Tuesday). Answer-invariant: core and envelope both select exactly the standup (16:00Z) and 1:1 (18:00Z). Excluded: Lunch with recruiter 19:30Z = 12:30pm PDT (afternoon, past the shared noon end), Gym today Tue 7:00am, and the trap: Trivia night 2026-07-15T04:00Z = Tue Jul 14 9:00pm PDT tonight — before the envelope start, but its UTC day is Jul 15, so a naive UTC 'tomorrow' window would count it. nl2time's 6am-noon reading [15T13:00Z, 15T19:00Z) contains the core and fits the envelope. get_next_event mocked consistently: next event after 8:00am Tue is tonight's Trivia (04:00Z).

scenarios.title: this-weekend-kolkata
scenarios.user: How many events do I have this weekend?

verifyPhrase.disagreementNote: Asked on a Friday, nl2time's primary reading of 'this weekend' is the PREVIOUS weekend (Jul 4-5); the upcoming weekend Jul 11-12 appears only as an alternative — the benchmark encodes the upcoming weekend, the ordinary conversational reading on a Friday

checks.note: Airport pickup Sat 3:30am + Wedding reception Sat 7pm + Cricket Sun 10am IST
The Sat 3:30am IST pickup (2026-07-10T22:00Z, UTC day Friday) must be counted as part of the weekend

scenarios.rationale: Now = FRIDAY Jul 10 2026, 4:30pm IST (UTC+5:30, non-integer offset). This weekend = Sat Jul 11 + Sun Jul 12 in Kolkata: [Jul 11 00:00 IST, Jul 13 00:00 IST) = [2026-07-10T18:30Z, 2026-07-12T18:30Z) — bounds land at half-hour UTC marks. In range: Airport pickup 2026-07-10T22:00Z = Sat Jul 11 3:30am IST (UTC day still Friday — dropped by naive UTC-weekend bounds [Jul 11T00Z, Jul 13T00Z)), Wedding reception 2026-07-11T13:30Z = Sat 7:00pm IST, Cricket match 2026-07-12T04:30Z = Sun 10:00am IST. Excluded: Office review 2026-07-10T12:00Z = Fri 5:30pm IST (today, pre-weekend) and Team offsite 2026-07-13T04:30Z = Mon 10:00am IST. Count = 3. get_next_event mocked consistently: next event after Fri 4:30pm IST is the 3:30am airport pickup.

scenarios.title: week-of-august-3rd
scenarios.user: How many meetings do I have the week of August 3rd?

verifyPhrase.disagreementNote: nl2time's primary reading resolves to the week of August 3rd 2025 — a year in the PAST relative to now (Jul 28 2026); the correct 2026 Sunday-start week appears only as an alternative — benchmark encodes the upcoming 2026 week under both week-start conventions

checks.note: Kickoff Mon Aug 3, Architecture review Wed Aug 5, All-hands Fri Aug 7

scenarios.rationale: Trap-free baseline. Now = TUESDAY Jul 28 2026, 9:15am EDT (UTC-4). Aug 3 2026 is a MONDAY. 'The week of August 3rd' admits Sunday-start (Sun Aug 2 - Sat Aug 8: [2026-08-02T04:00Z, 2026-08-09T04:00Z)) and Monday-start (Mon Aug 3 - Sun Aug 9: [2026-08-03T04:00Z, 2026-08-10T04:00Z)). In range under BOTH: Kickoff Mon Aug 3 10:00am EDT (14:00Z), Architecture review Wed Aug 5 2:00pm EDT (18:00Z), All-hands Fri Aug 7 1:00pm EDT (17:00Z) — no rows on the disputed edge days Sun Aug 2 or Sun Aug 9, so counts agree (3/3). Excluded: Sprint retro Fri Jul 31 3:00pm EDT (this week) and Quarterly planning Mon Aug 10 10:00am EDT (the week after; 2026-08-10T14:00Z is past both end bounds). All events are mid-day local, no UTC-day traps. get_next_event mocked consistently: next event after now is Friday's Sprint retro.

scenarios.title: thursday-review-wall-clock
scenarios.user: What time is my design review with the Berlin team on Thursday?

verifyPhrase.disagreementNote: nl2time's primary reading of bare 'Thursday' from a Monday is LAST Thursday (Jul 23); the upcoming Thursday Jul 30 appears only as an alternative — the question is present/future-tense ('What time IS my design review'), so the benchmark encodes upcoming Thursday

checks.note: Stored 17:30Z; user must hear 1:30 pm Eastern, not 5:30

scenarios.rationale: Now = MONDAY Jul 27 2026, 10:00am EDT (UTC-4). The question is future-tense, so 'on Thursday' = the upcoming Thursday Jul 30: [Jul 30 00:00 ET, Jul 31 00:00 ET) = [2026-07-30T04:00Z, 2026-07-31T04:00Z). In range: the Berlin design review 2026-07-30T17:30Z = Thu 1:30pm EDT (the answer; rejectUtcClock guards against reading 5:30 off the stored UTC value) and Budget check-in 19:00Z = 3:00pm EDT (different title, harmless). Excluded: LAST Thursday's design review Jul 23 at 15:00Z = 11:00am EDT — an agent that resolves to the past Thursday retrieves it and reports 11:00am, failing the clockTime check — and Dry cleaning pickup Tue Jul 28 6:00pm EDT. get_next_event mocked consistently: next event after Mon 10:00am is Tuesday's dry cleaning pickup (so the static tool cannot shortcut the search).

scenarios.title: meetings-last-week-chicago
scenarios.user: How many meetings did I have last week?

checks.note: Staff meeting Mon 6, Vendor call Wed 8, 1:1 Thu 9, Client debrief Fri 10 (7pm CDT, UTC-day Sat Jul 11)

scenarios.rationale: Now = WEDNESDAY Jul 15 2026, 8:05am CDT (UTC-5) — midweek on purpose so both week conventions agree on the interior. Bare 'last week' admits Sunday-start (en-US CLDR): Sun Jul 5 - Sun Jul 12 = [2026-07-05T05:00Z, 2026-07-12T05:00Z) (nl2time primary), and Monday-start (ISO): Mon Jul 6 - Mon Jul 13 = [2026-07-06T05:00Z, 2026-07-13T05:00Z). In range under BOTH: Weekly staff meeting Mon Jul 6 10:00am CDT, Vendor call Wed Jul 8 2:00pm, 1:1 with Dana Thu Jul 9 11:30am, and the trap row Client debrief call 2026-07-11T00:00Z = FRI Jul 10 7:00pm CDT (UTC day Saturday Jul 11 — still inside both readings, but a naive UTC Monday-start window [Jul 6T00Z, Jul 13T00Z) also holds it, so the count survives; its purpose is the local-day derivation in this rationale). No rows on the disputed edge days (Sun Jul 5, Sun Jul 12), so both tuples select the same 4 rows. Excluded: Sprint demo Tue Jul 14 (this week) and Board prep Thu Jul 2 (week before last). Count = 4.

scenarios.title: next-dentist-auckland
scenarios.user: When is my next dentist appointment?

checks.note: Stored Aug 3 21:00Z = Tuesday Aug 4, 9:00am NZST — answering 'August 3' is the UTC trap
Local weekday is Tuesday (UTC weekday is Monday)
If a time is given it must be 9:00 am local, not 21:00

scenarios.rationale: Pure time->NL. Now = THURSDAY Jul 30 2026, 9:00am NZST (UTC+12, southern winter). The next dentist appointment is stored 2026-08-03T21:00Z, which in Pacific/Auckland is TUESDAY Aug 4, 9:00am NZST — the UTC rendering (Monday Aug 3, 9:00pm) differs on day, weekday, and clock, all three trapped. The June 2 21:30Z row (= Wed Jun 3 9:30am NZST) is the previous appointment and must not be reported. get_next_event is mocked consistently with the rows: the next event overall after now is tomorrow's Team standup (2026-07-30T21:30Z = Fri Jul 31 9:30am NZST), not the dentist, so the agent must search. find_events rows carry full data whichever bounds the agent uses (args ungraded here); get_event_details returns the dentist event.

scenarios.title: invite-details-evening-rollover
scenarios.user: I just got an invite with id evt-4482. What day and time is that event?

checks.note: Stored Aug 15 00:30Z = Friday Aug 14, 8:30pm EDT — answering 'August 15' is the UTC trap
Local weekday is Friday (UTC weekday is Saturday)

scenarios.rationale: Pure time->NL, id lookup. Now = FRIDAY Jul 31 2026, 5:00pm EDT (UTC-4, month boundary). The invited event starts 2026-08-15T00:30Z = FRIDAY Aug 14, 8:30pm EDT — an evening event whose UTC day rolls over to Saturday Aug 15. Day, weekday, and clock all differ between UTC and local, so all three checks carry rejection traps. The invite is not yet on the calendar (find_events legitimately returns nothing for it); get_event_details is the intended path and takes no time argument, isolating the rendering direction.
